kicker: MiniMax Sparse Attention, from the paper

scenes.headline: How MiniMax lets each query pick its own blocks
scenes.sub: MiniMax Sparse Attention: exact attention over a fixed 2,048-token budget.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Magnolia! Long context is expensive because every token reads every past token. MiniMax Sparse Attention keeps attention exact, and reads less. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Keep attention exact, but let each query read only the 16 blocks a trained index picks for it: 2,048 tokens, at any length.
scenes.mark: the 16 blocks a trained index picks
scenes.say: Keep attention exact, but let each query read only the sixteen blocks a trained index picks for it. Two thousand and forty-eight tokens, however long the context.

steps.say: A cheap index branch scores every past token, then max-pools the scores into blocks of a hundred and twenty-eight.
It keeps the top sixteen blocks, a fixed two thousand and forty-eight tokens. The query's own block is always kept.
The main branch runs exact attention over just those blocks. Whole blocks keep memory reads contiguous, so a kernel turns the saving into real speed.

steps.note: a KL loss with stop-gradient: the backbone is untouched
steps.say: And the index is trained, not a heuristic. A loss aligns its scores with the real attention, and only the tiny index heads learn.

scenes.title: Each GQA group picks its own blocks

steps.label: Full attention: every group reads every block
steps.say: Sixty-four query heads share four KV heads, so there are four groups. Under full attention, every group reads every block.

steps.label: MSA: each group keeps its own few
steps.note: illustrative: the real budget is 16 blocks per query
steps.say: Under MSA, each group picks its own blocks from the same keys and values. Different heads see different parts of the past.

scenes.title: Speedup over full attention at 1M tokens
scenes.note: on H800; at 32k the advantage is barely 1.6x
scenes.say: At a million tokens, on the paper's own benchmark, prefill runs fourteen point two times faster, and decode seven point six, at on-par quality. At thirty-two K, the gain is small.

scenes.text: MSA keeps attention exact and full-range, and simply reads less of it, chosen per query and per group.
scenes.say: MSA keeps attention exact and full-range, and simply reads less of it, chosen per query and per group.

recap: Each GQA group picks its own
scenes.say: To recap: score the blocks, keep the top sixteen, and let every group choose its own.
